title: Customer Engagement Review Deck Templates and Renewal Sprint Tracker
body:
Purpose and scope:
This living doc contains two complementary deliverables for customer success managers: 1) lightweight deck templates for customer engagement reviews that scale across Standard (self-serve / SMB) and Enterprise accounts, and 2) a renewal sprint tracker pattern to run 8–12 week renewal plays. The emphasis is operational: replicable slide builds, clear owner actions, and fallout remediation steps so CSMs can run risk-first QBRs with prescriptive next steps.

Audience:
- CSMs preparing recurring account reviews (monthly/quarterly)
- AMs and Solutions Engineers joining pre-renewal engagements
- Customer Success leadership reviewing pipeline health and play effectiveness

How to use this file:
- Copy the appropriate deck template folder (Standard or Enterprise) into the customer folder for an account and fill placeholders.
- Sync the renewals tracker every Monday; update owner and next action.
- Use the playbook steps as the script for the pre-meeting prep call with the executive sponsor.

1) Deck templates overview (two variants)
A. Standard Review Deck (30–40 min; adoption-focused) — one-slide-per-topic fast flow
- Title + TL;DR (1) — 1-line health summary, renewal date, recommended ask (e.g., 12m renewal, expand to Dedicated)
- Current usage highlights (2) — topline metrics: active seats/routes, avg latency, token consumption vs forecast
- Key wins since last review (3) — bulletized wins with owners and outcomes (ROI metrics if available)
- Roadblocks / help needed (4) — prioritized list with owners, ETA to resolve
- Adoption playbook (5) — suggested next 90 days actions (onboarding, templates, enablement)
- Risk & renewal signal (6) — red/amber/green, open blockers that impact renewal
- Ask / next steps (7) — specific CTA and success criteria
- Appendix: how-to links and support contacts (8)

Speaker notes (Standard): Keep it short, highlight measurable outcomes, call out any production incidents or latency impacts that influence cost. Bring one customer quote if available.

B. Enterprise Review Deck (50–75 min; strategic + exec alignment) — multi-path narrative
Structure:
- Executive summary (1) — 3-line narrative: value delivered, risks, proposed renewal motion (term, capacity, SLAs)
- Business outcomes map (2) — tie Redwood metrics to customer KPIs (revenue lift, retention lift, query latency improvements)
- Technical health snapshot (3) — model variants in use, average p99 latency, error rates, infra footprint (GPUs, regions)
- Cost & utilization analysis (4) — per-route token economics, suggestions (batching/quantization) with estimated $/month savings
- Roadmap alignment (5) — feature work or integration asks with owners & timelines (product/engineering dependencies)
- Risk register & mitigation (6) — opened tickets, escalation path, SLA impact, fallback plan (compatible model variants)
- Renewal proposals (7) — 3 options: baseline renewal, committed capacity + discount, enterprise private deployment (summary table)
- Stakeholder asks & timeline (8) — procurement checklist, security review steps, legal/contract owners
- Appendix: detailed logs, runbooks, ticket links (9)

Speaker notes (Enterprise): Frame as business discussion; prepare two recommended motions (safe and stretch). Include cost/latency tradeoffs and a clear fallback policy (e.g., fallback to smaller model variant under capacity pressure). Bring SRE or solutions engineer to answer infra and security questions.

2) Slide-by-slide building blocks (reusable snippets)
- Health banner (one-line): "Health: GREEN — steady usage, 1 incident last 90d, renewal likely"
- One-line adoption metric card: metric name | period | delta vs last quarter | owner
- Risk badge: RED/AMBER/GREEN with 2-line rationale and top mitigation action
- Renewal motion table: Option | Term | Capacity | Est. savings | Action owner
- Ask card: "What we need from you" (3 bullets) + due date

3) Renewal sprint tracker pattern (copyable table rows for sheet)
Columns (recommended):
- Account
- Renewal date
- Current status (discovery | at-risk | negotiating | signed)
- Primary CSM
- Executive sponsor (email)
- Recommended motion (baseline/commit/private)
- Last engagement date
- Next action (text)
- Action owner
- Confidence score (1-10)
- Notes / blockers
- Jira/Support links

Example row (text form to paste into a sheet):
Redwood-HealthTech, 2025-02-18, negotiating, Asha Patel, j.smith@healthtech.com, committed-capacity, 2024-10-28, follow-up with procurement for SOW, Lina Ho, 6, security review delayed, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4233

Sprint cadence and rituals:
- Week 0: Kickoff with renewal map + owner assignments.
- Weeks 1–4: Customer discovery + technical remediation; track action completion in tracker.
- Weeks 5–8: Commercial proposal + procurement engagement; CSM builds negotiation playbook (discount levers, alternatives).
- Week 9–12: Finalize and secure signatures or pivot to retention/offboarding plan.

Escalation rules:
- Confidence score <= 4 at Week 4 -> auto-escalate to CS leadership + Solutions Eng.
- Any open security/compliance item -> engage Security team and add to risk register slide in Enterprise deck.

4) Playbook: meeting script and checklist (pre, during, post)
Pre-meeting (owner = CSM):
- Update deck with latest metrics and ticket links (2 days prior).
- Run a 30-min prep huddle with SE and AE to align asks and roles.
- Share pre-read to customer 48 hours before (1-page TL;DR and agenda).

During meeting:
- 0–5 min: Introductions and TL;DR (CSM)
- 5–15 min: Business outcomes and changes since last review (Customer exec + CSM)
- 15–30 min: Technical health and open items (SE / SRE)
- 30–45 min: Commercial proposal and ask (CSM + AE)
- 45–60 min: Close: next steps, owners, and timeline (all)

Post-meeting:
- Send meeting notes within 24 hrs with visible trackers and owner action list.
- Update renewal tracker row and set next check-in.
- If red or amber, schedule weekly progress calls.

5) Example follow-up templates (short snippets)
- Pre-read subject: "REVIEW: [Account] QBR pre-read — action items and agenda"
- Post-meeting subject: "Notes + Actions: [Account] QBR — next steps and owners"
Body snippet (post-meeting):
"Thanks all — summary below, owners in bold. Next meeting: [date]. Key action: procurement to share SOW draft by [date] (Owner: Lina Ho). Tracker link: [sheet link]."

6) Measurement and success criteria
Standard deck success metrics:
- % of reviews completed on schedule
- Time between review and signed renewal (median days)
- Average confidence score uplift after play (pre vs post)

Enterprise success metrics:
- Renewal attainment vs expected ARR for committed plays
- Avg time to close procurement hurdles (security/legal)
- Number of mitigation items resolved pre-renewal

7) Risks & mitigation examples (copyable lines)
- Risk: Security review stalls procurement -> Mitigation: Pre-submit architecture diagram + schedule SOC walkthrough within Week 2.
- Risk: Latency regression discovered -> Mitigation: Temporary routing to alternate region + prioritize model variant fallback.
- Risk: Unexpected cost spike -> Mitigation: Suggest quantization + temporary limit on non-critical routes; present projected $ impact.

8) Appendix: handy links and snippets to paste into decks
- Support ticket reference format: "CS-<account>-<ticket#>"
- Cost suggestion blurb: "Estimated savings if batching enabled: ~12–18% monthly token spend depending on route mix"
- Sample renewal options table (copy into slide):
  Option A: 12m baseline – no commit – standard rates
  Option B: 12m commit – 30% discount on infra + 6% professional services credit
  Option C: 24m committed Dedicated – priority capacity + SLA + onboarding bundle

Open questions / next edits:
- Add a one-page cheatsheet for Solutions Engineers with runbook links (Diego action)
- Convert the renewal tracker example into a pre-built Google Sheet template (Benji action)
- Validate cost-savings model with Finance for enterprise scenarios (Lina action)

Quick change log:
- 2024-08-15: Initial draft (Asha)
- 2024-09-02: Added Enterprise cost section (Lina)
- 2024-10-10: Incorporated escalation rules and tracker columns (Benji)
- 2024-11-02: Draft ready for peer review (collaborators added)

Notes to self (CSM style, informal):
- Keep slides light: execs want 3–4 key bullets.
- Bring measurable asks: procurement dates, security checklist items, and a clear single CTA.
- Use the tracker confidence score consistently across teams so leadership dashboard can roll up a reliable risk metric.

End of doc.
